triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed the additional standard deduction feeding 63(c)(1) from aged members only, omitting the blind additional amounts that 63(f)(2) grants, and returned basic + additional for every taxpayer, omitting 63(c)(6)'s rule that the standard deduction shall be zero for a married individual filing separately where either spouse itemizes, a nonresident alien, a short-period 443(a)(1) filer, and an estate/trust/common trust fund/partnership.
triage.triage_notes: Single module in the commit (plus its companion test and the encoding manifest). Commit subject says 'Encode 26 USC 63(c)' but the file already existed (45 lines pre-fix, 132 post-fix), so this is a correction of an existing encoding, not a first encoding. Two distinct missing-clause defects are fixed in one module: (a) the blind additional amount under 63(f)(2) — num_aged_members (count_where aged only) became num_additional_standard_deduction_conditions (aged count + blind count), and additional_std_ded_amount's source was re-attributed from 'IRC section 63(f)(1)(A), aggregated over qualifying individuals' to 'IRC section 63(c)(3)'; (b) the 63(c)(6) zero-out, added as a new standard_deduction_ineligible Judgment rule and an 'if standard_deduction_ineligible: 0 else: ...' gate on standard_deduction. The pre-fix additional_std_ded_amount was the only additional-deduction term in standard_deduction, so the aged-only count was a real fidelity gap in a claimed output, not merely added scope. I read the provision through resolve_provision.py (us/statute/26/63) and confirmed 63(f) 'Aged or blind additional amounts' paragraph (2) 'Additional amount for blind' and 63(c)(6)'s 'the standard deduction shall be zero'. The same commit also makes non-fidelity changes alongside: module summary replaced with the verbatim statute text, proof_validation: required added, proof atoms with excerpts and import hashes added, data_relation gains predicate/arguments, and num_* dtype changed Integer -> Count. No PR reviews, review comments, or issue comments exist on PR #25, and the commit body is empty, so the PR body bullets are the only stated reason. Still unrepresented after this commit: the 63(c)(5) dependent limitation on the basic standard deduction (out of scope here, worth noting for anyone screening later commits). PR #25 notes a dependency on axiom-rules-engine#35 for member_of_tax_unit namespacing, which is unrelated to the fidelity fix.
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempt fails on both prongs: the diff changes executable meaning (two formulas plus a new gating rule and new inputs), and the pre-fix encoding gave answers that contradict the cited text rather than merely lacking coverage. The pinned release shows 63(c)(1) defines the standard deduction "Except as otherwise provided in this subsection" as basic + additional, 63(c)(3) defines the additional standard deduction as "the sum of each additional amount to which the taxpayer is entitled under subsection (f)" (which includes 63(f)(2)'s blind amount), and 63(c)(6) says "the standard deduction shall be zero" for MFS-where-either-spouse-itemizes, nonresident aliens, 443(a)(1) short-period filers, and estates/trusts/common trust funds/partnerships. The pre-fix module's terminal rule `standard_deduction` (source "IRC section 63(c)(1)", formula `basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount`) therefore returned a nonzero deduction for every disqualified filer and understated it for blind taxpayers, so the fix adds clauses the source states rather than new scope the module never claimed. Both added pieces are missing statutory conditions, so unrepresented_clause is the right kind; no other kind (amount, boundary, polarity, entity, period) is the root of either change.
triage.verifier_quote:
-        formula: count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_aged_65_or_over)
+          count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_aged_65_or_over) + count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_blind)
-        formula: basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount
+          if standard_deduction_ineligible: 0 else: basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount
triage.verifier_notes: Checks run: read the bundle JSON and diff, the full parent file (0ca0e42ee9:statutes/26/63/c.yaml, 45 lines), the commit's test diff, the apply manifest, and the provision text via resolve_provision (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, resolved_text_sha256 7fa5f5d7...). Considered refutations and why they fail: (1) "new coverage, never claimed" — the pre-fix `additional_std_ded_amount` source string was scoped to 63(f)(1)(A) (aged), but the module's output rule `standard_deduction` claimed 63(c)(1) and its summary said the module "defines the standard deduction as the basic standard deduction plus any additional standard deduction," so a blind-only taxpayer got a wrong (too low) number and an NRA got a nonzero number; those are wrong answers against the cited text. (2) "stub replacement, nothing shipped to be wrong" — the parent version was a working, tested module (companion c.test.yaml asserted concrete values, e.g. joint_one_aged standard_deduction 33850), with prior history at 5e8437c60 / 34ad14677 / 516621eb7; not an empty placeholder. (3) "mechanical" — ruled out: formulas, dtype (Integer→Count), rule set, inputs, and expected test outputs all change (e.g. new nonresident_alien_standard_deduction_zero case asserts standard_deduction 0). Caveats for the reviewer: this commit is a full encoder re-generation (backend openai / gpt-5.5, manifest added here), so the fidelity fix is bundled with heavy provenance churn — statutory-text summary, proof atoms, import hashes, data_relation predicate/arguments — and the "Encode" subject hides that it modifies an existing module. Also, the post-fix module still omits 63(c)(5)'s dependent limitation and counts aged/blind over all tax-unit members rather than taxpayer-and-spouse per 63(f)(1)(B)/(2)(B); those are remaining gaps in the fix, not reasons to downgrade this classification.
